title: Part
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. In the first loop, draw the first line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.0208, 0.0), then draw the second line from (0.0208, 0.0) to (0.0208, 0.75), followed by the third line from (0.0208, 0.75) to (0.0, 0.75), and finally, the fourth line from (0.0, 0.75) back to the origin. After completing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Rotate the scaled sketch using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] and translate it using the translation vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Finally, extrude the sketch 0.0417 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. This results in a rectangular base with a length of 0.02083333333333333 meters, a width of 0.75 meters, and a height of 0.041666666666666664 meters.

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0417) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0417) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0208)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
